summary.name: agenttrace
summary.one_liner: agenttrace is a local-first terminal TUI and CLI that inspects coding-agent session logs for cost, tokens, latency, tool failures, health, and regressions.
keywords: how much did my coding agent spend
use_cases: Find the most expensive or slowest coding-agent runs
Diagnose hanging gaps, retry loops, and slow tool calls
Compare adjacent runs to explain a regression
Generate HTML or Markdown overview reports for PR review
Gate CI on health score, critical anomalies, or tool failure rate
summary.what_it_does:
agenttrace reads local logs from many coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Cline, Aider, Cursor exports, and others) plus generic JSON/JSONL traces and combines them into one timeline. It reports cost, tokens, latency, health, and tool failures per run, and lets you sort and filter sessions before opening a detail view. Diagnostics surface hanging gaps, slow tools, retry chains, repeated loops, and large parameters, with suggested next actions. The compare view diffs neighboring runs, and CLI commands can write HTML, Markdown, or JSON reports with health thresholds for CI. The page says it has no hosted backend and does not upload prompts.</what_it_does>
<parameter name="pricing">open source
notable: Single Rust binary with a terminal TUI built on ratatui and crossterm
Reads logs from many agents locally with no hosted backend and no prompt upload
Evidence labels (Detailed, Aggregate, Limited) show how much data each source provides
CLI reports and gates for PR review and CI, including health and tool-failure thresholds
caveats: The page shows a redacted static sample, not current telemetry
Platform support beyond the terminal is not explicitly detailed on the page
